_metadata.title: D38999 Pinout Rules, Protocol Wiring, and Gauge-to-Current Dataset
_metadata.purpose: Reference dataset for the D38999 toolbox. Covers: (1) new protocols not in connector_engineering_reference.json, (2) comprehensive twisted-pair adjacency rules including both-connector constraints, (3) wire gauge current capacity and parallel-pin distribution tables with worked examples.

wire_gauge_current_capacity._note: Wire and contact current ratings for aerospace (MIL-W-22759 PTFE wire) and MIL-DTL-38999 contacts. MIL-spec ratings are lower than AWG commercial tables due to bundling, altitude, and temperature constraints. Always verify with manufacturer datasheet and applicable installation standard (e.g. AS50881).

mil_dtl_38999_contact_single_ratings._source: MIL-DTL-38999 Table IV, sea level, 25°C ambient, single contact

mil_spec_wire_ampacity_bundled._source: AS50881 Table VII / MIL-HDBK-522, bundled in harness, 70°C insulation, 25°C ambient
mil_spec_wire_ampacity_bundled._note: These are WIRE ampacity values. Contact rating (above) may be the limiting factor — always use the lower of the two.

22_awg.note: Typical 22 AWG in bundled aerospace harness

derating_factors._note: Multiply contact single-contact rating by this factor when N contacts in same connector are simultaneously energized.

by_temperature_ambient._note: Additional multiplier for ambient temperature above 25°C

by_altitude._note: Current derating for altitude (reduced convection cooling)

parallel_pin_distribution._principle: When a single contact cannot carry the required load, the current must be distributed across multiple parallel contacts. All contacts must be the same gauge, same wire length, and same crimp quality to ensure equal sharing. A single contact opening (N-1 failure) must not overload the remaining contacts beyond 80% of their derated capacity.
parallel_pin_distribution._return_balance: Every supply contact requires an equal number of return contacts of the same gauge. Unbalanced supply/return is a common dangerous error.

worked_examples.scenario: 5A continuous load, #22D contacts, sea level, 25°C, 10 total energized contacts
20A load, 28 VDC, #20 contacts, sea level, 25°C, 20 total energized contacts
worked_examples.alternative: Use 3x #12 contacts (23A × 0.85 derating × 0.75 margin = 14.7A each; 2 contacts = 29.3A > 20A, N-1 ok for 3 contacts). 3 supply + 3 return = 6 contacts total, more compact.
worked_examples.recommendation: Prefer 3x #12 for 20A (6 contacts total) over 7x #20 (14 contacts)

worked_examples.scenario: 50A load, #12 contacts, sea level, 25°C, 15 total energized contacts
worked_examples.recommendation: Use 6 supply + 6 return #12 contacts. Alternatively use #8 contacts (46A rated, derated 0.66 = 30.4A; 2 contacts = 60.7A, N-1: 30.4A > 50A*0.8=40A, need 3 contacts of #8)

worked_examples.scenario: 100A load, #8 contacts, sea level, 25°C, 20 total energized contacts

parallel_contact_rules: All paralleled contacts MUST be the same gauge/size
All paralleled wires MUST be the same length (within 10%) — resistance difference causes current imbalance
All crimp connections MUST use the same qualified crimp tool, die, and process
Distribute paralleled contacts physically across the insert — do not group all in adjacent cavities
Each supply contact needs an equal number of return contacts of the same size
Design for N-1 survival: if one contact opens, remaining contacts must not exceed 80% of their derated capacity
Apply a minimum 25% margin over the calculated requirement before N-1 check
Do NOT parallel contacts of different sizes on the same rail
Fretting corrosion from vibration can increase contact resistance unpredictably over time

voltage_considerations._note: Contact gauge affects current capacity, not voltage rating directly. MIL-DTL-38999 contacts are rated to 200V DC (Series III) or per applicable slash sheet. Larger loads at higher voltages require fewer contacts since P=V×I (same power, higher voltage = lower current).

quick_reference_table._note: Minimum contacts needed (supply only) for given load and contact size. Does NOT include derating or N-1 margin — apply those factors in actual design. Always add equal number of return contacts.
quick_reference_table.reminder: Add derating (typ 0.60–0.85 depending on energized contacts), 25% design margin, N-1 check, AND equal return contacts. Actual contacts needed will be 1.5–2× the table values.

twisted_pair_adjacency_rules._principle: A differential pair (+ and − signals) MUST be routed on a twisted pair cable. Both wires of the pair MUST terminate into ADJACENT cavities in the connector. This applies to BOTH connectors in a mated pair — the plug AND the receptacle must each have the P and N of every differential pair in adjacent, physically neighboring cavities.
why_it_matters: Differential pairs rely on equal and opposite fields to cancel EMI emissions and reject common-mode noise.
If P and N are in non-adjacent cavities, the cable twist must be untwisted before entry, creating an unbalanced stub that radiates and picks up noise.
For high-speed signals (Ethernet, USB, HDMI TMDS, RS-485, CAN), a non-adjacent assignment causes signal integrity failure: increased common-mode noise, eye diagram violations, bit errors.
The cable between the two connectors may physically be a twisted pair, but if the connector cavity assignment breaks the pair apart, the twist benefit is lost inside the connector.
For MIL-STD-1553, ARINC 429, and similar mil/avi buses, splitting the pair in the connector creates coupling paths that violate bus electrical specs.

both_connectors_constraint.explanation: When a plug (connector A) mates with a receptacle (connector B), the cavity numbering is shared — cavity 'A' on the plug mates to cavity 'A' on the receptacle. If the differential pair occupies cavities 'A' and 'B' (adjacent) on the plug, those same cavities 'A' and 'B' will be adjacent on the receptacle. So planning pair assignments by cavity IDs automatically satisfies both connectors simultaneously.
both_connectors_constraint.plug_vs_receptacle_orientation: WARNING: When viewed from the MATING FACE, plug and receptacle appear as mirror images. When viewed from the WIRE SIDE (installation side), the orientation is different. Always use cavity LABEL (letter/number ID) to plan pin assignments — never use physical position drawings without verifying plug vs receptacle face orientation.
both_connectors_constraint.mirror_face_rule: Never assign a pair based on physical position drawings without confirming whether the drawing shows the mating face or wire side, and whether it shows the plug or receptacle. Use the cavity label (e.g. 'A', '1', '7', 'AA') as the common reference between both connectors.
both_connectors_constraint.adjacency_verification: After assigning cavities, verify the insert arrangement drawing confirms the chosen cavities are physically neighboring in the insert. For circular inserts, adjacent means same row AND neighboring column position, or confirmed by the insert arrangement's physical layout.

insert_adjacency_identification._note: D38999 insert arrangements have named cavity positions. 'Adjacent' means physically neighboring — sharing a common wall or separated by minimal distance. The insert arrangement drawing is the authoritative source. Common adjacent pairs are determined by the circular geometry: inner ring, middle ring, outer ring positions.
insert_adjacency_identification.general_rule: For any insert arrangement, cavities that share a row in the insert layout are the best candidates for differential pairs. Consult the specific insert arrangement drawing (e.g. MIL-DTL-38999 Appendix or manufacturer insert spec) to confirm adjacency.
avoid: Never place P on inner ring and N on outer ring — these are NOT adjacent
Never place P and N on opposite sides of the insert face
Never place P and N with a power contact between them — proximity to high current is also a coupling concern
Never assume alphabetical order = physical adjacency

pair_assignment_checklist: 1. Identify all differential pairs for the interface (see protocol pinout rules below)
2. Look up the insert arrangement drawing for the selected connector
3. Identify groups of physically adjacent cavities (neighboring positions in the insert)
4. Assign each differential pair to one such adjacent group
5. Verify the SAME cavity labels are used on BOTH the plug and receptacle wiring diagrams
6. Mark all pair assignments on both plug and receptacle ICD drawings
7. Keep power contacts away from high-speed diff pair groups (use ground/return as physical buffer)
8. For shielded pairs: include a dedicated ground/drain contact immediately adjacent to or near the pair

mil_std_1553.note: Dual-redundant: 2 pairs (Bus A and Bus B) for redundant system

ethernet_2500base_t.note: Same 4-pair topology as 1000BASE-T with tighter channel margin

ethernet_5gbase_t.note: Same 4-pair topology as 1000BASE-T with higher SI sensitivity

rj48c_t1_e1.note: Balanced telecom receive and transmit pairs

mil_std_1553.name: MIL-STD-1553
mil_std_1553.typical_use: Avionics and military systems data bus: aircraft, spacecraft, ground vehicles
mil_std_1553.typical_cable: 78Ω twinax cable per MIL-C-17 or equivalent
mil_std_1553.max_bus_length: No hard limit in standard; practical ~30m (100ft) main bus due to propagation delay vs rise time

termination.note: At each physical end of bus only

mil_std_1553.redundancy: Dual redundant buses (Bus A and Bus B) — all devices connect to both
mil_std_1553.protocol: Command/Response: Bus Controller (BC) → Remote Terminal (RT). One BC active at a time. Up to 31 RTs.

pair_groups.notes: MUST be adjacent in connector. Keep as twinax cable twist to connector entry.
Second redundant bus. Same adjacency rule applies.

d38999_notes: BUS_A_P and BUS_A_N MUST be in adjacent cavities
BUS_B_P and BUS_B_N MUST be in adjacent cavities (if dual-redundant)
Keep twinax cable twist as close to the contacts as possible — minimize untwisted stub
Use shielded backshell with 360° shield termination
Bus terminators (78Ω) must be AT the bus coupler at the physical end of the main bus — not at the stub connector
Stub connectors must NOT have termination resistors unless this connector is the physical bus end
For transformer-coupled stubs: isolation transformer and resistors are in the bus coupler box, not in the circular connector itself
Shielding: ≥75% optical coverage per MIL-STD-1553
MIL-DTL-38999 circular connectors are the standard for airborne installations
warnings: Do NOT terminate the stub connector — only terminate at the physical ends of the main bus cable
Star topology is NOT allowed — bus topology only
Direct-coupled stubs longer than 1 ft (0.3m) can distort main bus waveforms
Transformer-coupled stubs preferred for fault isolation and noise rejection
Both Bus A and Bus B must be fully independent — share no grounds, shields, or routing paths

arinc_429.name: ARINC 429
arinc_429.typical_use: Commercial and transport aircraft avionics data bus
arinc_429.direction: Single transmitter → up to 20 receivers. Full duplex requires separate TX and RX buses.

pair_groups.notes: Must be adjacent in connector. Each bus direction (TX and RX) is a separate pair.

d38999_notes: DATA_A and DATA_B MUST be adjacent cavities
TX and RX are on separate physical wire pairs — each pair must be in adjacent cavities
Include shield/drain wire contact near the pair
Do NOT share the signal return with chassis ground — keep bus ground floating from chassis
Bus driver/receiver ICs (e.g. HOLT HI-8578, DDC ACT4488) must be co-located with equipment, not at the connector
Each connected subsystem is a separate receiver tap — do not daisy-chain without proper loading analysis
Maximum 20 receivers on a single bus before signal loading degrades
For long harness runs, use ≥75% braid or foil+braid shielding
warnings: ARINC 429 is unidirectional — TX and RX use separate wire pairs and separate connector cavity pairs
Do not exceed 20 receiver loads on one transmitter
Cable shield should be grounded at ONE point only (usually at transmitter end) to avoid ground loops
Rise/fall time specification (1.5–2.5μs for high speed, 10–20μs for low speed) must be met by driver IC

afdx_arinc_664.name: AFDX (Avionics Full-Duplex Switched Ethernet) / ARINC 664 Part 7
afdx_arinc_664.typical_use: Modern commercial aircraft avionics data network (A380, B787, A350, A400M)
afdx_arinc_664.redundancy: Dual redundant networks (Network A and Network B) — same physical layout, independent

pair_groups.notes: TX pair MUST be adjacent. Typically Cat 5e STP cable.
RX pair MUST be adjacent. Keep separate from TX pair for full duplex.

d38999_notes: TX+ and TX- MUST be in adjacent cavities
RX+ and RX- MUST be in adjacent cavities
For dual-redundant AFDX: Network A and Network B must be on SEPARATE connectors or clearly isolated groups
Cable must be Cat 5e or better; STP (shielded twisted pair) preferred for harsh environments
For EMC-critical applications, use shielded backshell with 360° shield termination
AFDX end-system ICs (e.g. Curtiss-Wright, DDC AFDX modules) handle MAC/VL framing — not in connector
Standard D38999 signal contacts adequate for 100 Mbps (100BASE-TX bandwidth ~31 MHz) in validated harness
warnings: AFDX is NOT generic Ethernet — it adds deterministic scheduling, VL policing, and redundancy at the protocol layer
Cable quality matters: Cat 5e STP minimum, shielded backshell required for harsh environments
Both Network A and Network B must be fully independent (separate cables, shields, and connector cavities)
Max cable length 100m per IEEE 802.3; harness routing should stay well under this

spacewire.name: SpaceWire
spacewire.typical_use: Spacecraft on-board data networks, satellite instruments, NASA JWST, GOES-R
spacewire.encoding: Data-Strobe (DS) encoding — clock embedded in strobe transitions

signals.name: DIN_P
signals.description: Data In positive (from remote to this node)

signals.name: GND
signals.description: Ground (not connected in harness; grounded on PCB connector only)

pair_groups.notes: Receive data pair. MUST be adjacent.
Receive strobe pair. MUST be adjacent.
Transmit data pair. MUST be adjacent.
Transmit strobe pair. MUST be adjacent.

d38999_notes: Four differential pairs total: DIN, SIN, DOUT, SOUT — each pair must be adjacent in connector
SpaceWire defines its own 9-pin Micro-D connector; when using D38999, map signals to adjacent cavity groups
PCB ground (pin 3 in Micro-D) must NOT be connected in harness — only short to chassis at PCB end
Receiver termination (100Ω) is internal to LVDS receiver chip — no external termination at connector
Use individually shielded twisted pairs for each of the 4 differential pairs
Cable: typically LVDS cable, 100Ω characteristic impedance
Data-strobe encoding eliminates the need for separate clock signal, but strobe pair must be adjacent just like data pair
warnings: SpaceWire has 4 differential pairs — all 4 pairs MUST have adjacent cavity assignments
In/out direction: DIN/SIN are inputs from remote node; DOUT/SOUT are outputs to remote node — direction crosses in cable
Fault tolerant: SpaceWire routers can route around failed links — requires correct multi-port wiring
Space qualification: connector, wire, and termination must meet relevant ECSS/MIL environmental requirements

lvds_generic.name: LVDS (Low-Voltage Differential Signaling)
lvds_generic.typical_use: High-speed point-to-point serial: Camera Link, FPD-Link, proprietary video, instrument buses

pair_groups.notes: Adjacent cavities mandatory. Keep twist as close to connector as possible.

fpd_link_18bit.description: FPD-Link / LVDS 18-bit RGB video (3 data pairs + 1 clock pair)
fpd_link_18bit.note: Each data pair is 7-bit serialized at 7× pixel clock. All 4 pairs MUST have adjacent cavity assignments.

d38999_notes: LVDS P and N MUST be in adjacent cavities
Termination resistor (100Ω) at receiver end — inside equipment, not at connector
For multipoint (M-LVDS): current doubles (≤12mA), same adjacency rules
Shielded cable strongly recommended for EMC compliance
Match cable impedance to termination (both 100Ω typical)

ethernet_10gbase_t.name: 10GBASE-T (10 Gigabit Ethernet over copper)

pair_groups.notes: All pairs bidirectional — echo cancellation in PHY. MUST be adjacent.

d38999_notes: All 4 pairs bidirectional simultaneously (unlike 1000BASE-T which also uses all 4 pairs bidirectionally but at much lower per-pair bandwidth)
400 MHz bandwidth per pair — far exceeds what standard D38999 signal contacts handle. Twinax or Quadrax contacts strongly recommended.
For short runs (<1m) with validated cable assembly, high-quality signal contacts may work — requires signal integrity validation.
PHY-level echo cancellation and alien crosstalk cancellation are built into 10GBASE-T chips — cable crosstalk budget is tight.
All 4 pairs must be in adjacent cavity pairs, distributed across the insert to minimize alien crosstalk between pairs.
Shield must be terminated at both ends with 360° backshell
Latency is 2–4μs (higher than fiber-based 10GbE) due to FEC processing
warnings: 10GBASE-T is the most electrically demanding copper Ethernet standard. Standard D38999 inserts are likely NOT adequate without qualified high-speed contacts.
4-pair alien crosstalk cancellation requires careful cable-to-connector transition design
SI validation (eye diagram, insertion loss, return loss, crosstalk) mandatory before production
Power consumption of 10GBASE-T PHY is higher than fiber alternatives — thermal consideration in sealed enclosures

poe_power_over_ethernet.name: Power over Ethernet (PoE)
poe_power_over_ethernet.typical_use: Powering IP cameras, VoIP phones, WAPs, sensors over Ethernet cable
poe_power_over_ethernet.power_delivery_method: Common-mode current on differential pairs. Power does not interfere with data because differential signal is symmetric. Power extracted via center-tap of Ethernet transformer at each end.

signals.name: BI_DC_P
signals.description: Pair C (spare for 10/100, data for GbE)

signals.name: BI_DD_P
signals.description: Pair D (spare for 10/100, data for GbE)

poe_power_over_ethernet.contact_size_power: 22D for Type 1/2 (≤600mA); upgrade to #20 for Type 3/4 at 960mA per pair in harsh environments
d38999_notes: PoE data pairs carry both signal AND power — use standard signal contacts for Type 1/2 (350–600mA per pair per wire direction)
For Type 3/4 (960mA): at 57V, that's ~55W on two conductors. Verify thermal performance, especially in bundled harness.
All 4 pairs must be in adjacent cavity pairs (same rules as 10/100/1000BASE-T)
Power negotiation (PSE detection, classification) occurs over the data pairs — requires correct PCB-level PoE controller circuitry
Shield termination at both ends — PoE PSE/PD equipment requires this for EMC
Temperature rise in cable bundles is significant for 4PPoE — IEEE 802.3bt requires temperature derating for bundled cables
warnings: PoE voltage (44–57V DC) is above the 30V safety threshold in many jurisdictions — hazardous voltage labeling may be required
Do NOT connect PoE PSE equipment to non-PoE-aware devices without checking for compatibility (may damage older equipment)
4-pair PoE (Type 3/4) requires all 4 pairs energized — cable and connector must handle ~4× the current per wire of Type 1
Thermal management of cable bundles is important — high PoE current raises insulation temperature

analog_4_20ma.name: 4-20 mA Current Loop (Industrial Analog)
analog_4_20ma.typical_use: Industrial sensors, process control (temperature, pressure, flow), PLC I/O

range_mA.note: 4mA=0% range, 20mA=100% range, <4mA or >20mA indicates fault or loop break

analog_4_20ma.max_loop_resistance_ohm: Depends on supply voltage: (V_supply - V_sensor_min) / 0.020. Typical 250Ω for 24V supply.

signals_2wire.name: LOOP_P
signals_2wire.description: Loop supply (+24V side from controller or transmitter)

signals_2wire.name: LOOP_N
signals_2wire.description: Loop return (0V side, current measured here)

d38999_notes: Low current (4-20mA) — #22D contacts are adequate for the signal itself
Supply power wire may carry significant current for multi-channel systems — verify total load
For noise immunity in harsh environments, use shielded twisted pair (shield grounded at one end only)
Keep signal wires away from high-current switching loads to avoid induced noise
HART protocol can ride on 4-20mA loop (1.2kHz FSK) — same wiring applies

analog_0_10v.name: 0–10 V Analog Voltage
analog_0_10v.typical_use: Industrial control signals, HVAC, lighting, DAC outputs
d38999_notes: Single-ended — susceptible to ground noise. Keep analog return separate from digital and power ground where possible.
For long cable runs or noisy environments, convert to 4-20mA current loop for better noise immunity
Shield cable if signal accuracy matters
Current drawn is typically <10mA — #22D contact is adequate

aes3_digital_audio.name: AES3 / AES/EBU Digital Audio
aes3_digital_audio.typical_use: Professional audio equipment, broadcast, studio interconnect

pair_groups.notes: Must be adjacent in connector. 110Ω termination at receiver.

d38999_notes: AES3_P and AES3_N MUST be adjacent cavities
Cable impedance is 110Ω (different from 75Ω coax or 100Ω Ethernet) — use correct cable type
Receiver termination is 110Ω differential inside audio equipment — no external termination at connector
Carries 2 audio channels (stereo or dual mono) multiplexed with metadata
Multiple AES3 pairs can share a connector — each pair must be assigned to adjacent cavities

analog_audio_balanced.name: Balanced Analog Audio (IEC 61938 / AES48)
analog_audio_balanced.typical_use: Professional audio microphone, line-level, or speaker signals
d38999_notes: Audio P and N MUST be adjacent for balanced noise rejection
Phantom power (48V, 6.8 mA per conductor) can be carried on balanced audio pair — verify contact current rating
For speaker-level signals: may require larger contacts depending on amplifier current output
Keep away from digital switching signals to avoid intermodulation noise

discrete_28vdc.name: MIL-STD-704 28 VDC Discrete (Discrete Signal)
discrete_28vdc.typical_use: Aircraft discrete signals: switch status, relay drive, lamp test, mode selection

logic_levels.open: treated as low or high depending on circuit (pull-up or pull-down)

d38999_notes: #22D contact adequate for most discrete signals (5A rated, typical load <100mA)
Relay coil drive loads: verify contact current if driving relays directly (typ 100mA–500mA coil current)
28V discretes must be filtered/debounced in software or hardware for mechanical switch inputs
Keep high-speed data signal wires away from 28V discretes to avoid coupling

thermocouple.name: Thermocouple Signal
thermocouple.typical_use: Temperature measurement, engine monitoring, thermal management
thermocouple.contact_material_note: Standard copper/nickel contacts introduce thermoelectric EMF at each junction. For accurate measurement: use thermocouple-grade extension wire with matching alloy contacts, or use isothermal terminal blocks at connector with cold-junction compensation.
d38999_notes: TC_P and TC_N should be in adjacent cavities to minimize differential loop area and EMI pickup
Thermocouple signal is microvolts to millivolts — extremely sensitive to EMI and contact material
Avoid placing thermocouple wires near high-current or switching power wires
Cold-junction compensation must account for connector temperature when using standard contacts
Twisted pair extension wire should remain twisted to within 5cm of connector entry

pwm_discrete_signal.name: PWM / Digital Discrete Signal (5V/3.3V TTL)
pwm_discrete_signal.typical_use: Servo control, motor speed, LED dimming, digital discrete I/O
d38999_notes: Single-ended signal — for long cables or noisy environments, convert to RS-422 differential
Ground reference MUST accompany the signal in the same connector
Keep PWM signal wires twisted with their return in the harness to minimize radiated emissions
High-frequency PWM (>100kHz) can be a significant EMI source — shield cable for frequencies >10kHz

design_rules.action: Assign P and N of same pair to physically adjacent connector cavities
design_rules.applies_to: BOTH plug and receptacle (use same cavity labels)
design_rules.details: Non-adjacent pair assignment is a wiring error regardless of interface. Check the insert arrangement drawing for adjacency before assigning cavities.

design_rules.action: Use the same cavity labels for the differential pair on both the plug AND the receptacle wiring diagrams
design_rules.details: Cavity labels (A, B, C, etc.) are shared between mating connectors. Adjacent cavities on the plug are adjacent on the receptacle. If cavity 'A' is adjacent to 'B' on the insert, assign pair to A+B on BOTH connectors.

design_rules.condition: Multiple differential pairs in same connector
design_rules.action: Assign each pair to its own adjacent group. Keep pair groups separated by at least one ground contact.
design_rules.details: Crosstalk between pairs is reduced when pair groups are separated by ground contacts. For high-speed pairs (USB 3.x, 10GbE, DisplayPort), use Twinax contacts per pair.

design_rules.condition: Power rail current exceeds single-contact rating
design_rules.action: Parallel multiple contacts of same size. Apply derating, 25% margin, and N-1 survival check.
design_rules.details: See wire_gauge_current_capacity.parallel_pin_distribution for worked examples and formula.

design_rules.action: Number of return contacts MUST equal number of supply contacts. Same size, same wire length.
design_rules.details: An imbalanced supply/return ratio creates a single-point bottleneck on the return path, causing voltage drop, overheating, and common-mode noise injection.

design_rules.condition: High-current power AND high-speed differential pairs in same connector
design_rules.action: Separate power contacts from signal contacts. Use ground contacts as physical buffer.
design_rules.details: Switching transients on power conductors couple into adjacent high-speed signal pairs. Place ground/return contacts between power group and signal group in the insert layout.

design_rules.action: Do NOT install bus termination resistors at stub connector. Termination only at main bus physical ends.
design_rules.details: Stub connectors must be left open-circuit (with dust caps) when not connected. Only two terminators in the entire system — at the physical ends of the main bus cable.

design_rules.action: Ground shield at ONE end only (typically the transmitter end or LRU chassis). Do not ground both ends.
design_rules.details: Grounding both ends of an ARINC 429 shield creates a ground loop that can inject noise. Single-point grounding prevents this.

design_rules.action: Always confirm whether the reference drawing shows mating face or wire/installation side, and whether it shows plug or receptacle.
design_rules.details: Plug and receptacle mating faces appear mirrored. A drawing of the plug mating face has opposite left-right orientation from the plug wire side. Confusion causes systematic pair assignment errors on one connector.

design_rules.condition: Power rail voltage > 30V (e.g. 48V PoE, 270V DC, 115V AC)
design_rules.action: Apply appropriate electrical safety standards (hazardous voltage labeling, insulation coordination, creepage/clearance verification)
design_rules.details: MIL-DTL-38999 Series III is rated to 200V RMS. For higher voltages, verify applicable slash sheet and dielectric withstanding voltage specs.

protocol_cross_reference._note: Cross-reference to companion files for protocols already fully documented elsewhere
